chunks: He said: Abu al-Qasim Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh - may Allah have mercy on him - reported from his father, from Sad ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hannan ibn Sudayr, from his father, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, when the believer and his rights were mentioned. Abu Abdillah turned to me and said: O Abu al-Fadl, shall I not tell you about the state of the believer with Allah? I said: Yes, tell me, may I be your ransom.

So he said: When Allah seizes the soul of the believer, his two angels ascend to heaven and say: O Lord, Your servant and what an excellent servant! The Majestic, the Compeller says: Descend to the world and remain at the grave of My servant, and glorify Me and praise Me and declare My oneness and magnify Me, and write that for My servant until I resurrect him from his grave.

Then he said to me: Shall I not tell you more? I said: Yes. He said: When Allah resurrects the believer from his grave, there comes out with him an image leading him. Whenever the believer sees a terror from the terrors of the Day of Judgment, the image says to him: Do not be alarmed and do not grieve, and receive glad tidings of delight and honor from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And it continues to give him glad tidings of delight and honor from Allah until he stands before Allah, Glory be to Him, and He reckons him an easy reckoning, and orders him to Paradise, and the image before him.

So the believer says to the image: May Allah have mercy on you, what an excellent companion! You came out with me from my grave, you have not ceased giving me glad tidings of delight and honor from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until that was so. So who are you? The image says: I am the delight that you brought upon your believing brother in the world. Allah created me from it to give you glad tidings.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for bringing joy to believers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq describes the afterlife of a believer.
